findings.F1: The book loses on the few bars it acts on: it is short on only 2.3% of bars (136 of 5,842), and on those bars the coin rose +0.41% the next day on average, against +0.12% on all bars, so each short bar lost 0.19% before fees.
findings.F2: The short is gone almost as soon as it opens. Short runs last 1.24 bars on average, with a median of 1 and a maximum of 3, because the new-low condition holds only on the bar of the low. The result is 121 trades averaging 1.2 days, winning 31% of the time, with a mean net result of −0.74%. Fees took a further 0.146 of book value on top of a gross loss of −0.255.
findings.F3: The divergence carries no information. Over 32 spaced events the excess 20-bar return was −0.58% (t −0.16). Recomputed divergence lows (40) against non-divergence new lows (66) differ by Welch t between −1.26 and +0.03 at every horizon from 1 to 20 days.
findings.F4: The tested grading runs backwards: at divergence lows, the deeper the 30-day decline, the larger the next rise. The 30-day return correlates −0.37 with the 5-day forward return and −0.41 with the 10-day forward return. The deepest third (30-day return −33%, n 14) rose +2.1% over 5 days and +4.4% over 10 days. The mildest third (−8.6%, n 14) fell −3.6% over 5 days and −3.7% over 10 days.
findings.F5: The rebound after deep declines does not depend on the divergence. Non-divergence new lows in the deepest third (30-day return −29%, n 22) rose +5.9% over 5 days and +7.4% over 10 days. The middle and mild thirds rose −0.7% to +0.5% over 5 days.

ideas.idea: When a coin's close makes a new 30-day low, the deeper its 30-day decline into that low, the larger its rise over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A new low reached after a steep 30-day fall is a reason to refuse a short and to consider a long for about ten days.
ideas.name: deep new lows rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin's close makes a new 30-day low while its 14-day RSI is above its reading at the previous low in that window, the price keeps falling over the next 10 days, and the shallower the coin's 30-day decline into that low, the larger the further fall.
ideas.consequence: A divergence low reached after only a mild 30-day slide is a reason to keep a short for days, while one reached after a steep slide is not.
ideas.name: shallow divergence lows keep falling
